sentences.text: Lucasuchus is an extinct genus belonging to the group of armored reptiles known as aetosaurs.

This animal possessed elongated horns on its lateral osteoderms, a feature shared with other members of the subfamily Desmatosuchinae. The paramedian osteoderms of Lucasuchus feature large conical projections, whereas Longosuchus has only low pyramidal bosses. Unlike Longosuchus, Lucasuchus lacks notches on the spikes of its lateral osteoderms.
The genus Lucasuchus was named in 1995 in honor of the American paleontologist Spencer G. Lucas.
Fossils of Lucasuchus have been discovered in the Bull Canyon Formation of the Dockum Group in Quay County, New Mexico.

Researchers have debated whether Lucasuchus represents a sexual dimorph of Longosuchus meadei or an ontogenetic stage of that species. Despite the debate, several characteristics suggest that Lucasuchus is a distinct species rather than a morphological variation of Longosuchus meadei.
